package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.ViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import kotlinx.coroutines.delay
import kotlinx.coroutines.isActive
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch

class JsonParsingViewModel : ViewModel() {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 // Start a timer to update elapsed time while parsing is in progress
 val timerJob = viewModelScope.launch {
 while (isActive) {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 delay(10) // Update approximately every 10ms for smoother UI
 }
 }
 
 try {
 // TODO: Add actual JSON parsing logic here
 
 } finally {
 timerJob.cancel()
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.LargeJsonModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.decodeFromStream

class JsonParsingViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 try {
 withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
 val context = getApplication<Application>().applicationContext
 val inputStream = context.assets.open("large_file.json")
 
 // Parse JSON to list of LargeJsonModel
 val largeJsonModels: List<LargeJsonModel> = inputStream.use { stream ->
 json.decodeFromStream(stream)
 }
 
 // You can do something with the parsed models if needed
 }
 } finally {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This implementation:
1. Changes to `AndroidViewModel` to access application context
2. Creates a `Json` instance with `ignoreUnknownKeys = true` for more robust parsing
3. Uses `Dispatchers.IO` for background processing
4. Opens the JSON file from assets using the application context
5. Uses Kotlin's `kotlinx.serialization` to parse the JSON stream directly into a list of `LargeJsonModel` objects
6. Properly closes the input stream with `use` block
7. Records the total time taken for the parsing operation

Note: Make sure the JSON file is placed in the assets folder at `app/src/main/assets/large_file.json`.

package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.R
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.LargeJsonModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json
import kotlinx.serialization.json.decodeFromStream

class JsonParsingViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 try {
 withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
 val context = getApplication<Application>().applicationContext
 val inputStream = context.resources.openRawResource(R.raw.large_file)
 
 // Parse JSON to list of LargeJsonModel
 val largeJsonModels: List<LargeJsonModel> = inputStream.use { stream ->
 json.decodeFromStream(stream)
 }
 
 // You can do something with the parsed models if needed
 }
 } finally {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This implementation:
1. Uses `context.resources.openRawResource()` to access the file from the `res/raw` directory
2. References the resource using `R.raw.large_file` (assuming the filename is `large_file.json` without the extension in the resource ID)
3. Keeps the rest of the implementation the same, parsing the JSON into a list of `LargeJsonModel` objects
4. Still properly measures and records the time taken for the parsing operation

Note: Make sure the JSON file is placed in the raw resources directory at `app/src/main/res/raw/large_file.json`. The resource ID will be `large_file` (without the .json extension).

package com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.ui.screen.json_parsing

import android.app.Application
import androidx.compose.runtime.IntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.asIntState
import androidx.compose.runtime.mutableIntStateOf
import androidx.lifecycle.AndroidViewModel
import androidx.lifecycle.viewModelScope
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.R
import com.augieafr.benchmarkapp.data.LargeJsonModel
import kotlinx.coroutines.Dispatchers
import kotlinx.coroutines.launch
import kotlinx.coroutines.withContext
import kotlinx.serialization.decodeFromString
import kotlinx.serialization.json.Json

class JsonParsingViewModel(application: Application) : AndroidViewModel(application) {
 private val _timeStamp = mutableIntStateOf(0)
 val timeStamp: IntState = _timeStamp.asIntState()
 
 private val json = Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true }
 
 fun startParsing() = viewModelScope.launch {
 _timeStamp.value = 0
 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 
 try {
 withContext(Dispatchers.IO) {
 val context = getApplication<Application>().applicationContext
 val inputStream = context.resources.openRawResource(R.raw.large_file)
 
 // Read the JSON content as a string
 val jsonString = inputStream.bufferedReader().use { it.readText() }
 
 // Parse JSON to list of LargeJsonModel using Kotlin Serialization
 val largeJsonModels: List<LargeJsonModel> = json.decodeFromString(jsonString)
 
 // You can do something with the parsed models if needed
 }
 } finally {
 _timeStamp.value = (System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime).toInt()
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

This implementation:
1. Uses `context.resources.openRawResource()` to access the file from the `res/raw` directory
2. Reads the entire JSON content as a string using `bufferedReader().readText()`
3. Uses Kotlin Serialization's `Json.decodeFromString()` to parse the JSON string into a list of `LargeJsonModel` objects
4. Configures the JSON parser to ignore unknown keys for more robust parsing
5. Properly measures and records the time taken for the parsing operation

Note: Make sure your `LargeJsonModel` class and its nested classes are properly annotated with `@Serializable` for Kotlin Serialization to work correctly.

 55	 _isLoading.value = true

 59	 try {

 67

 69	 val deleteResult = benchmarkDeleteOperation()
 70	 results.add(deleteResult)
 71	
 72	 _benchmarkResults.value = results

 74	 } catch (e: Exception) {
 75	 _errorMessage.value = "Benchmark failed: ${e.message}"
 76	 } finally {
 77	 _isLoading.value = false
 78	 }
 79	 }

 82	 private suspend fun benchmarkInsertOperation(): DatabaseBenchmarkResult {
 83	 val startTime = System.currentTimeMillis()
 84	 noteRepository.addNotes(listNote) // Insert random notes
 85	 val duration = System.currentTimeMillis() - startTime
 86	
 87	 return DatabaseBenchmarkResult(
 88	 operation = "Insert ${listNote.size} Notes",
 89	 duration = duration,
 90	 recordCount = listNote.size,
 91	 status = "Success"
 92	 )
 93	 }

 99	
 100	 return DatabaseBenchmarkResult(

2. **Updated DatabaseOperationTestScreen.kt:**

### Key Features of the New Component:

```kotlin
@Composable
private fun NotesCountInputSection(
 notesCount: Int,
 onNotesCountChange: (Int) -> Unit,
 onGenerateNotes: () -> Unit,
 isLoading: Boolean
) {
 Card(
 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
 colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(
 containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceVariant
 )
 ) {
 Column(
 modifier = Modifier
 .fillMaxWidth()
 .padding(16.dp),
 verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)
 ) {
 Text(
 text = "Notes Configuration",
 style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
 fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold
 )

 Row(
 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
 horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
 verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
 ) {
 OutlinedTextField(
 value = notesCount.toString(),
 onValueChange = { newValue ->
 newValue.toIntOrNull()?.let { count ->
 onNotesCountChange(count)
 }
 },
 label = { Text("Number of Notes") },
 keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
 modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
 enabled = !isLoading,
 singleLine = true
 )

 ElevatedButton(
 onClick = onGenerateNotes,
 enabled = !isLoading,
 modifier = Modifier.width(140.dp)
 ) {
 Icon(
 imageVector = Icons.Default.Add,
 contentDescription = null
 )
 Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(4.dp))
 Text("Generate")
 }
 }

 Text(
 text = "Generate random notes to be inserted into the database for benchmarking",
 style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
 )
 }
 }
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### How to Use:

1. **Open the app** and navigate to "Database Operation Test"
2. **Set the number of notes** you want to generate in the text field (default: 1000)
3. **Click "Generate"** to create the random notes in memory
4. **Click "Run Full Database Benchmark"** to test database operations with the generated notes

### Features:

- ✅ **Input validation**: Only accepts numeric input
- ✅ **Minimum value protection**: Ensures at least 1 note is generated
- ✅ **Loading state handling**: Disables input during operations
- ✅ **Material 3 design**: Consistent with the existing UI
- ✅ **Responsive layout**: Works well on different screen sizes
- ✅ **Clear user guidance**: Includes descriptive text

## Summary

I have successfully created a composable component to set how many notes to be inserted into the database. Here's what was implemented:

### Changes Made:

1. **Updated DatabaseOperationTestViewModel.kt:**
 - Added `_randomNotesCount` state flow with default value of 1000
 - Exposed `randomNotesCount` as a public state flow
 - Added `updateRandomNotesCount(count: Int)` function to update the count
 - Added `generateRandomNotes()` function to trigger note generation
 - Made the existing `setRandomNotes` function work with the new state management

2. **Updated DatabaseOperationTestScreen.kt:**
 - Added necessary imports for text input and keyboard options
 - Created `NotesCountInputSection` composable component with:
 - A text field for entering the number of notes
 - A "Generate" button to create the notes
 - Proper validation and error handling
 - Material 3 design consistent with the existing UI
 - Integrated the new component into the main screen layout

### Key Features of the New Component:

````kotlin path=app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/database_operation_test/DatabaseOperationTestScreen.kt mode=EXCERPT
@Composable
private fun NotesCountInputSection(
 notesCount: Int,
 onNotesCountChange: (Int) -> Unit,
 onGenerateNotes: () -> Unit,
 isLoading: Boolean
) {
 Card(
 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
 colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(
 containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceVariant
 )
 ) {
 Column(
 modifier = Modifier
 .fillMaxWidth()
 .padding(16.dp),
 verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)
 ) {
 Text(
 text = "Notes Configuration",
 style = MaterialTheme.typography.titleMedium,
 fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold
 )

 Row(
 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
 horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp),
 verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
 ) {
 OutlinedTextField(
 value = notesCount.toString(),
 onValueChange = { newValue ->
 newValue.toIntOrNull()?.let { count ->
 onNotesCountChange(count)
 }
 },
 label = { Text("Number of Notes") },
 keyboardOptions = KeyboardOptions(keyboardType = KeyboardType.Number),
 modifier = Modifier.weight(1f),
 enabled = !isLoading,
 singleLine = true
 )

 ElevatedButton(
 onClick = onGenerateNotes,
 enabled = !isLoading,
 modifier = Modifier.width(140.dp)
 ) {
 Icon(
 imageVector = Icons.Default.Add,
 contentDescription = null
 )
 Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(4.dp))
 Text("Generate")
 }
 }

 Text(
 text = "Generate random notes to be inserted into the database for benchmarking",
 style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
 )
 }
 }
}
````

### How to Use:

1. **Open the app** and navigate to "Database Operation Test"
2. **Set the number of notes** you want to generate in the text field (default: 1000)
3. **Click "Generate"** to create the random notes in memory
4. **Click "Run Full Database Benchmark"** to test database operations with the generated notes

### Features:

- ✅ **Input validation**: Only accepts numeric input
- ✅ **Minimum value protection**: Ensures at least 1 note is generated
- ✅ **Loading state handling**: Disables input during operations
- ✅ **Material 3 design**: Consistent with the existing UI

- ✅ **Clear user guidance**: Includes descriptive text

### 2. **Smart Benchmark Button Control**

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/database_operation_test/DatabaseOperationTestScreen.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin

ElevatedButton(
 onClick = onRunBenchmark,

) {
 Icon(

 )

}

if (!isReady && !isLoading) {

</augment_code_snippet>

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/database_operation_test/DatabaseOperationTestViewModel.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
private val _notesGenerated = MutableStateFlow(false)
val notesGenerated = _notesGenerated.asStateFlow()

/**
 * Update the count of random notes to be generated
 */
fun updateRandomNotesCount(count: Int) {
 _randomNotesCount.value = count.coerceAtLeast(1) // Ensure minimum of 1
 _notesGenerated.value = false // Reset generated status when count changes
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### Key Features:

✅ **Status Indicator**: The header now shows clear status messages:
- **Ready**: "Ready to benchmark (X notes prepared)" in primary color
- **Not Ready**: "Not ready - Please generate notes first" in error color

✅ **Smart Button Control**: The "Run Full Database Benchmark" button is:
- **Enabled** only when notes have been generated AND not loading
- **Disabled** when no notes are generated or when loading

✅ **User Guidance**: When not ready, helpful text appears below the button explaining what to do

✅ **State Management**: The app properly tracks:
- Whether notes have been generated
- When the count changes (resets the generated status)
- Loading states

### User Flow:

1. **Initial State**: Status shows "Not ready", benchmark button is disabled
2. **Set Count**: User enters number of notes in the input field
3. **Generate Notes**: User clicks "Generate" button
4. **Ready State**: Status shows "Ready to benchmark (X notes prepared)", benchmark button becomes enabled
5. **Change Count**: If user changes the count, status resets to "Not ready" until they generate again

The implementation ensures users cannot run benchmarks without first preparing the test data, providing a better user experience and preventing potential errors.

## Summary

I have successfully created a comprehensive **Animation Performance Test** screen that measures and compares UI rendering performance under sustained animation load. Here's what was implemented:

### **Test Scenario Implementation**

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/animation_test/AnimationTestScreen.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
@Composable
fun AnimationTestScreen(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
 val viewModel: AnimationTestViewModel = viewModel()
 val isAnimating by viewModel.isAnimating.collectAsState()
 val animationProgress by viewModel.animationProgress.collectAsState()
 val benchmarkResults by viewModel.benchmarkResults.collectAsState()
 val errorMessage by viewModel.errorMessage.collectAsState()
 val animationReady by viewModel.animationReady.collectAsState()
```
</augment_code_snippet>

### **Key Features Implemented**

#### **1. 20 Animated Elements**
- **Initial State**: 20 cards stacked at the center of the screen
- **Final State**: Elements arranged in a 4×5 grid layout
- **Visual Design**: Each card contains a small image and text label

#### **2. Simultaneous Multi-Property Animation**
For each of the 20 elements, the following properties animate concurrently:

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/animation_test/AnimationTestScreen.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
// Animation values
val animatedPosition = remember {
 Animatable(
 Offset(
 with(density) { centerX.toPx() },
 with(density) { centerY.toPx() }
 ),
 Offset.VectorConverter
 )
}
val animatedRotation = remember { Animatable(0f) }
val animatedScale = remember { Animatable(0.8f) }
val animatedAlpha = remember { Animatable(0.5f) }
```
</augment_code_snippet>

- ✅ **Translation**: X and Y coordinates from center to grid position
- ✅ **Rotation**: 0° to 360° rotation during movement
- ✅ **Scale**: 80% to 100% size transformation
- ✅ **Alpha**: 0.5 to 1.0 opacity fade-in

#### **3. Performance Tracking**

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/animation_test/AnimationTestViewModel.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
data class AnimationBenchmarkResult(
 val testName: String,
 val duration: Long,
 val frameCount: Int,
 val averageFps: Float,
 val droppedFrames: Int,
 val status: String
)
```
</augment_code_snippet>

The system tracks:
- **Animation Duration**: Total time for complete animation sequence
- **Frame Count**: Number of frames rendered during animation
- **Average FPS**: Calculated performance metric
- **Dropped Frames**: Performance degradation indicator

#### **4. Smart UI Controls**

<augment_code_snippet path="app/src/main/java/com/augieafr/benchmarkapp/ui/screen/animation_test/AnimationTestScreen.kt" mode="EXCERPT">
```kotlin
// Status and Progress
val statusText = when {
 isAnimating -> "Animating... ${(animationProgress * 100).roundToInt()}%"
 animationReady -> "Ready to start animation test"
 else -> "Preparing animation..."
}
```
</augment_code_snippet>

- **Status Indicator**: Shows current animation state
- **Progress Bar**: Real-time animation progress
- **Control Buttons**: Start, Reset, and Clear Results
- **Results Display**: Detailed performance metrics

#### **5. Staggered Animation Effect**
```kotlin
// Stagger animations slightly for visual effect
val delay = element.id * 50L
val animationDuration = 2000 + delay.toInt()
```

Each element starts with a 50ms delay multiplied by its ID, creating a visually appealing cascade effect while maintaining the stress test requirements.

### **How to Use the Animation Test**

1. **Open the app** and navigate to "Animation Performance Test"
2. **Initial View**: See 20 cards stacked in the center with instructions
3. **Start Test**: Tap "Start Animation" to begin the performance test
4. **Watch Animation**: All 20 elements simultaneously animate to grid positions
5. **View Results**: After completion, see detailed performance metrics
6. **Reset/Repeat**: Use Reset button to return to initial state
7. **Clear Results**: Remove previous test results

### **Performance Metrics Displayed**

- **Test Name**: "20 Element Grid Animation"
- **Duration**: Total animation time in milliseconds
- **Average FPS**: Frames per second during animation
- **Frame Count**: Total frames rendered
- **Status**: Success/Failure indicator

### **Stress Test Characteristics**

This implementation creates significant rendering load through:
- **20 simultaneous animations** (high element count)
- **4 concurrent property animations** per element (translation, rotation, scale, alpha)
- **Complex calculations** for grid positioning
- **Continuous frame tracking** for performance measurement
- **Real-time progress updates**

The test is designed to reveal performance differences between Native Android and KMP implementations by stressing the rendering pipeline with sustained, complex animations that challenge the UI framework's ability to maintain smooth 60fps performance.

The animation test is now fully integrated into the app and ready for performance benchmarking!

 63	 _errorMessage.value = null

 83	 } finally {
 84	 _isLoading.value = false
 85	 }
 86	 }

fun AnimationTestScreen(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
 var isAnimating by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
 var animationStarted by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
 var completedAnimations by remember { mutableStateOf(0) }

 val allAnimationsComplete = completedAnimations >= totalAnimations
 
 // Reset counter when starting new animation

 if (isAnimating) {

 }

 LaunchedEffect(allAnimationsComplete) {
 if (allAnimationsComplete && isAnimating) {

 )

 val isAlphaComplete: Boolean = false
) {
 val isComplete: Boolean
 get() = isPositionComplete && isRotationComplete && isScaleComplete && isAlphaComplete
}

@Composable

) {

 animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = animationDuration),
 finishedListener = {
 animationState = animationState.copy(isPositionComplete = true)
 onAnimationStateChange(animationState)
 }
 )

}

I've successfully implemented approach #4 (Counter-Based) to track when all animations have completed. Here's a summary of the changes made:

## Key Changes Made:

### 1. **Animation Completion Tracking**
- Added `completedAnimations` state to count finished animations
- Added `totalAnimations` constant (20 cards)
- Added `allAnimationsComplete` computed property

### 2. **State Management**
- **Reset Logic**: When starting a new animation, the counter resets to 0
- **Completion Logic**: When all animations complete, `isAnimating` is automatically set to false
- **Progress Tracking**: Real-time progress display showing "X/20" completed animations

### 3. **UI Enhancements**
- **Progress Display**: Shows "Progress: X/20" in the header when animations are running
- **Enhanced Status Indicator**: 
 - Gray: Ready
 - Yellow: Animating 
 - Blue: Partial completion
 - Green: All complete
- **Reset Button**: Appears after animations complete to restart the test

### 4. **Animation Completion Detection**
- Each `AnimatedCard` now has an `onAnimationComplete` callback
- Uses the `finishedListener` on the alpha animation as the completion trigger
- Prevents duplicate completion calls with `hasCompletedAnimation` flag
- Resets the completion flag when new animations start

### 5. **Callback Chain**
```
AnimatedCard (finishedListener) → onAnimationComplete() → completedAnimations++ → 
allAnimationsComplete check → isAnimating = false
```

## How It Works:

1. **Start Animation**: User clicks "Start Animation Performance Test"
2. **Progress Tracking**: Each card's alpha animation completion triggers the callback
3. **Counter Updates**: `completedAnimations` increments for each finished card
4. **Auto-Complete**: When `completedAnimations >= 20`, `isAnimating` automatically becomes false
5. **Reset Option**: User can click "Reset Animation" to start over

## Benefits:

- **Accurate Detection**: Tracks actual animation completion, not just estimated timing
- **Real-time Progress**: Users can see exactly how many animations have finished
- **Visual Feedback**: Status indicator and progress counter provide clear state information
- **User Control**: Reset button allows easy restart of the animation test

The implementation is robust and handles edge cases like preventing duplicate completion callbacks and properly resetting state between animation cycles. You can now reliably detect when all 20 card animations have completed!

I've modified the animation logic so that the elements will stay in their final animated state after the animation completes. Here's what changed:

## Key Change:

Instead of using just `isAnimating` to determine the target values, I now use `isAnimating || hasCompletedAnimation`. This means:

### Before (elements returned to initial state):
```kotlin
targetValue = if (isAnimating) finalValue else initialValue
```

### After (elements stay in final state):
```kotlin
targetValue = if (isAnimating || hasCompletedAnimation) finalValue else initialValue
```

## What This Means:

1. **During Animation**: Elements animate from initial to final positions
2. **After Animation Completes**: Elements remain in their final positions:
 - **Position**: Cards stay in the 4×5 grid layout
 - **Rotation**: Cards stay rotated 360° (which visually looks normal)
 - **Scale**: Cards stay at full size (1.0)
 - **Alpha**: Cards stay fully opaque (1.0)

3. **Only on Reset**: When the user clicks "Reset Animation", `hasCompletedAnimation` gets reset to `false`, and elements return to their initial stacked state

## Behavior Flow:

1. **Initial State**: All cards stacked in center, small scale, semi-transparent
2. **Animation**: Cards move to grid positions with rotation, scaling, and fading
3. **Completion**: Cards stay in final grid positions ✅ (NEW BEHAVIOR)
4. **Reset**: Cards return to initial stacked state
5. **Ready for Next Animation**: Cycle can repeat

Now your animation test will show the final result of the performance test, with all 20 cards remaining in their organized 4×5 grid layout after the animation completes!

 56	@Composable
 57	fun AnimationTestScreen(modifier: Modifier = Modifier) {
 58	 var isAnimating by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
 59	 var animationStarted by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }
 60	
 61	 Column(
 62	 modifier = modifier
 63	 .fillMaxSize()
 64	 .padding(16.dp),
 65	 verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(16.dp)
 66	 ) {
 67	 // Header Section
 68	 AnimationHeaderSection(
 69	 isAnimating = isAnimating,
 70	 animationStarted = animationStarted
 71	 )
 72	
 73	 // Action Buttons
 74	 AnimationActionButtons(
 75	 onStartAnimation = {
 76	 isAnimating = true
 77	 animationStarted = true
 78	 },
 79	 isAnimating = isAnimating
 80	 )
 81	
 82	 LargeSpace()
 83	
 84	 // Animation Container
 85	 AnimationContainer(
 86	 isAnimating = isAnimating,
 87	 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxSize()
 88	 )
 89	 }
 90	}

 92	@Composable
 93	private fun AnimationHeaderSection(
 94	 isAnimating: Boolean,
 95	 animationStarted: Boolean
 96	) {
 97	 Card(
 98	 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
 99	 colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(
 100	 containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surfaceVariant
 101	 )
 102	 ) {
 103	 Column(
 104	 modifier = Modifier
 105	 .fillMaxWidth()
 106	 .padding(16.dp)
 107	 ) {
 108	 Text(
 109	 text = "Animation Performance Test",
 110	 style = MaterialTheme.typography.headlineSmall,
 111	 fontWeight = FontWeight.Bold
 112	 )
 113	
 114	 MediumSpace()
 115	
 116	 Row(
 117	 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth(),
 118	 horizontalArrangement = Arrangement.SpaceBetween,
 119	 verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
 120	 ) {
 121	 Column {
 122	 Text(
 123	 text = "Elements: 20 cards",
 124	 style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
 125	 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
 126	 )
 127	 Text(
 128	 text = "Grid: 4×5 layout",
 129	 style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodyMedium,
 130	 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant
 131	 )
 132	 }
 133	
 134	 // Status Indicator
 135	 Row(
 136	 verticalAlignment = Alignment.CenterVertically
 137	 ) {
 138	 Box(
 139	 modifier = Modifier
 140	 .size(12.dp)
 141	 .background(
 142	 color = when {
 143	 isAnimating -> Color.Yellow
 144	 animationStarted -> Color.Green
 145	 else -> Color.Gray
 146	 },
 147	 shape = RoundedCornerShape(6.dp)
 148	 )
 149	 )
 150	 Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(8.dp))
 151	 Text(
 152	 text = when {
 153	 isAnimating -> "Animating"
 154	 animationStarted -> "Complete"
 155	 else -> "Ready"
 156	 },
 157	 style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
 158	 fontWeight = FontWeight.Medium
 159	 )
 160	 }
 161	 }
 162	 }
 163	 }
 164	}

 166	@Composable
 167	private fun AnimationActionButtons(
 168	 onStartAnimation: () -> Unit,
 169	 isAnimating: Boolean
 170	) {
 171	 Column(
 172	 verticalArrangement = Arrangement.spacedBy(12.dp)
 173	 ) {
 174	 // Start Animation Button
 175	 ElevatedButton(
 176	 onClick = onStartAnimation,
 177	 enabled = !isAnimating,
 178	 modifier = Modifier.fillMaxWidth()
 179	 ) {
 180	 Icon(
 181	 imageVector = Icons.Default.PlayArrow,
 182	 contentDescription = null
 183	 )
 184	 Spacer(modifier = Modifier.width(8.dp))
 185	 Text("Start Animation Performance Test")
 186	 }
 187	
 188	 // Show explanation when animating
 189	 if (isAnimating) {
 190	 Text(
 191	 text = "Animation in progress - testing simultaneous translation, rotation, alpha, and scale transformations",
 192	 style = MaterialTheme.typography.bodySmall,
 193	 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurfaceVariant,
 194	 modifier = Modifier.padding(top = 4.dp)
 195	 )
 196	 }
 197	 }
 198	}

 200	@Composable
 201	private fun AnimationContainer(
 202	 isAnimating: Boolean,
 203	 modifier: Modifier = Modifier
 204	) {
 205	 val density = LocalDensity.current
 206	
 207	 // Card dimensions
 208	 val cardSize = 60.dp
 209	 val cardSpacing = 8.dp
 210	
 211	 // Grid configuration (4 columns, 5 rows)
 212	 val columns = 4
 213	 val rows = 5
 214	
 215	 // Calculate grid dimensions
 216	 val gridWidth = (cardSize * columns) + (cardSpacing * (columns - 1))
 217	 val gridHeight = (cardSize * rows) + (cardSpacing * (rows - 1))
 218	
 219	 Box(modifier = modifier) {
 220	 // Create 20 animated cards
 221	 repeat(20) { index ->
 222	 val row = index / columns
 223	 val column = index % columns
 224	
 225	 // Calculate target position in grid (relative to container center)
 226	 val targetOffsetX = (column * (cardSize + cardSpacing).value).dp - gridWidth / 2 + cardSize / 2
 227	 val targetOffsetY = (row * (cardSize + cardSpacing).value).dp - gridHeight / 2 + cardSize / 2
 228	
 229	 AnimatedCard(
 230	 index = index,
 231	 isAnimating = isAnimating,
 232	 targetOffset = Offset(
 233	 with(density) { targetOffsetX.toPx() },
 234	 with(density) { targetOffsetY.toPx() }
 235	 ),
 236	 cardSize = cardSize,
 237	 modifier = Modifier.align(Alignment.Center)
 238	 )
 239	 }
 240	 }
 241	}
 242	
 243	@Composable
 244	private fun AnimatedCard(
 245	 index: Int,
 246	 isAnimating: Boolean,
 247	 targetOffset: Offset,
 248	 cardSize: androidx.compose.ui.unit.Dp,
 249	 modifier: Modifier = Modifier
 250	) {
 251	 // Animation duration with slight stagger for visual effect
 252	 val animationDuration = 2000 + (index * 50) // 2-3 seconds with stagger
 253	
 254	 // Animate position
 255	 val animatedOffset by animateOffsetAsState(
 256	 targetValue = if (isAnimating) targetOffset else Offset.Zero,
 257	 animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = animationDuration),
 258	 label = "position_$index"
 259	 )
 260	
 261	 // Animate rotation (full 360 degree rotation)
 262	 val animatedRotation by animateFloatAsState(
 263	 targetValue = if (isAnimating) 360f else 0f,
 264	 animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = animationDuration),
 265	 label = "rotation_$index"
 266	 )
 267	
 268	 // Animate scale (start small, grow to normal size)
 269	 val animatedScale by animateFloatAsState(
 270	 targetValue = if (isAnimating) 1f else 0.3f,
 271	 animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = animationDuration),
 272	 label = "scale_$index"
 273	 )
 274	
 275	 // Animate alpha (fade in effect)
 276	 val animatedAlpha by animateFloatAsState(
 277	 targetValue = if (isAnimating) 1f else 0.7f,
 278	 animationSpec = tween(durationMillis = animationDuration),
 279	 label = "alpha_$index"
 280	 )
 281	
 282	 Card(
 283	 modifier = modifier
 284	 .size(cardSize)
 285	 .offset {
 286	 IntOffset(
 287	 x = animatedOffset.x.roundToInt(),
 288	 y = animatedOffset.y.roundToInt()
 289	 )
 290	 }
 291	 .scale(animatedScale)
 292	 .rotate(animatedRotation)
 293	 .alpha(animatedAlpha)
 294	 .border(
 295	 width = 1.dp,
 296	 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.outline,
 297	 shape = RoundedCornerShape(8.dp)
 298	 ),
 299	 colors = CardDefaults.cardColors(
 300	 containerColor = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.surface
 301	 ),
 302	 elevation = CardDefaults.cardElevation(defaultElevation = 4.dp)
 303	 ) {
 304	 Column(
 305	 modifier = Modifier
 306	 .fillMaxSize()
 307	 .padding(4.dp),
 308	 horizontalAlignment = Alignment.CenterHorizontally,
 309	 verticalArrangement = Arrangement.Center
 310	 ) {
 311	 Image(
 312	 painter = painterResource(id = R.drawable.ic_launcher_foreground),
 313	 contentDescription = "Card ${index + 1}",
 314	 modifier = Modifier.size(32.dp)
 315	 )
 316	 Text(
 317	 text = "Card ${index + 1}",
 318	 fontSize = 8.sp,
 319	 textAlign = TextAlign.Center,
 320	 color = MaterialTheme.colorScheme.onSurface,
 321	 maxLines = 1
 322	 )
 323	 }
 324	 }
 325	}
